rows.description: A worker gets comments like not good enough with no example and feels both stung and lost. Without specifics, feedback informs nothing and simply hurts.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Giving feedback that can be used [Response]
rows.description: A wise reviewer names what works, points to a concrete spot that needs change, and says why. Specific, timely, kind feedback lets the receiver act on it instead of defending.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: A teenager working on a maths problem or a code bug tries things at random, hoping something works, and cannot say what fixed it. Panic favours motion over thinking and leaves nothing learned.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.subtype: Blaming the tool or the world [Actor]
rows.description: A student stuck on an error insists the computer or the question is wrong before checking their own assumptions. Most stubborn faults sit in what was assumed and never verified.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: A wise problem solver first makes the fault repeatable, narrows where it lives, changes one thing at a time and notes each result. Writing down steps stops circular guessing and helps when tired.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: A stuck worker takes a short walk or explains the problem aloud to a friend and often sees the error immediately. Stepping back breaks tunnel vision and is a technique, not a surrender.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: A young engineer facing a live failure with people watching feels heart racing and narrowed thinking, and is tempted to change many things at once. Stress shrinks working memory exactly when clarity is needed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: Colleagues notice one calm person asking simple questions while others speculate loudly. Calm methodical narrowing down, not brilliance, is usually what resolves the trouble.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Debugging and problem solving under pressure
rows.description: A person fixing a fault while managers keep asking for updates feels their attention split and their work slowed. A single update channel and a set interval protect the fixer's focus.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager choosing a stream or course delays for months hoping for a clear sign. Certainty is rarely available, and the waiting itself narrows the options and increases anxiety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
